title: Danishmendids
capsule: The Danishmendids were a Turkic dynasty established in north-central Anatolia following the Seljuk victory at Manzikert (1071), ruling from Sivas, Tokat, and Niksar. Danishmend Gazi's most celebrated coup came in 1100 when he captured Bohemond I of Antioch, holding him until 1103 for a substantial ransom; a Danishmendid-Seljuk alliance then crushed the Crusade of 1101. The dynasty split between Sivas and Malatya branches after Mehmed's death in 1142, leaving it vulnerable to Seljuk expansion; Kilij Arslan II absorbed Sivas by the 1170s and Malatya fell in 1178, ending Danishmendid rule. The dynasty's resistance to the First and Second Crusades made it a significant check on Crusader expansion in Anatolia.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The dynasty's core territory in Cappadocia and Pontus is reasonably attested in Byzantine, Armenian, and Arabic chronicles, but peripheral boundaries with Seljuk and Byzantine domains fluctuated and remain imprecisely mapped.
